title: Becoming like God
hookLine: the Orthodox speak of salvation as union with God, like iron glowing in fire

lines: A BAR OF BLACK IRON IN THE COALS.
cards: A blacksmith pushes a bar of black iron into the coals and leaves it there. At first nothing seems to happen. Then a dull red creeps along it.
Then orange. Then it glows so bright you can't tell where fire stops and iron begins. Pull it out, and it lights the room.
Touch it, and it burns like fire. And yet it's still iron. It hasn't turned into fire.
It has the fire all through it. Orthodox Christian teachers have reached for this picture to say what salvation finally is. Not only a verdict.

teach.b: Theosis is a Greek word: becoming godlike, sharing in God's own life. Yesterday asked how I can be right with God. This asks how I can be filled with God.

Day one thousand eighty met a line from the second letter of Peter, and the Orthodox build on it: God has given promises "that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature." Partakers. Sharers.
Exodus has a picture of it. Moses comes down the mountain after speaking with God, and "Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him." He didn't know.
Still a man, and shining. Now the careful part. Becoming godlike never means becoming God.

teach.h: STILL IRON: NEVER GOD BY NATURE.
teach.b: The iron never stops being iron. Orthodox teachers distinguish God's inner being, which no creature can share, from God's life and light, which God pours out freely.
One old saying: what God is by nature, a person may become by grace. Where can you see this light? Orthodox Christians point to another mountain.

teach.h: HIS FACE DID SHINE AS THE SUN.
teach.b: When Jesus was transfigured, Matthew says, "his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light." They see that light as a glimpse of where human life is headed.
John's first letter keeps the ending open: "it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him."
Western Christians have their own words for this hope, like union with God and seeing him face to face. The Orthodox say theosis, and picture it glowing.

how: Orthodox Christians speak of theosis as the goal of the Christian life, pursued through the sacraments, prayer such as the Jesus Prayer, fasting and love, and they celebrate the Transfiguration as a major feast, a sign of the light they hope to share.

o: sharing in God's own life by grace, while staying human
a soul dissolving into God and losing itself completely
the Greek study of God and of what he is like

games.q: iron in the fire — tap the pairs.
p: his face shone, and he wist not
his face did shine as the sun

s: theosis means a person becomes God by nature
the iron stays iron. Orthodox teachers say we share God's life and light, never God's inner being.
second Peter speaks of sharing the divine nature
"that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature."
in Exodus, Moses knew his face was shining
"Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him."

games.q: you're Peter on the mountain. Jesus' face shines like the sun and his clothes are white as light. what do you say?
o: let's build three shelters and stay here.
let's run and tell the others right now.
games.why: Peter offers to make three tabernacles. he wants to stay in the light. some readers hear in that the hope of theosis.

practice: If you can, sit by a sunny window, light a candle, or turn toward a lamp, and let the light fall on your face and hands. You don't have to do anything to be warmed.
If you pray, simply stay near God, the way iron stays in the coals; if you don't, let the light do its quiet work.

wordCard.voice: Theosis. The Orthodox word for salvation as union with God: sharing God's life and light, like iron glowing in fire, while staying iron.

orig.note: Greek: becoming godlike, sharing in God's life. a word of the Greek church fathers.

carryVoice: Your line: iron in the fire. Still iron, full of fire. Until tomorrow.
